Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking the time last week. To recap our immediate ask: we need a Dedicated offering that satisfies the following for our payments platform by the end of Q2:

- Separate reserved GPU pools in three regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) with per-region throughput guarantees.
- Active DR/replication options (near-synchronous KV replication or periodic warm standby) — options and cost estimates.

Option 2 (recommended for compliance & performance): dedicated pools per region with optional replication add-on (near-sync for hot KV vs warm-standby). Higher base cost, predictable latency, and simpler in-region logs.

I'll attach an initial quote and a commit-model spreadsheet for you to iterate on. Quick question: which regions are highest priority (we listed three above) and do you have a target committed spend range (monthly)? That will help me size the pools.

Draft commercial options (numbers are illustrative):

Option A — Shared logical pool with regional ingress
- Single committed capacity equivalent to N GPUs (pool spread across AZs).
- Pro: ~10–15% lower base cost.
- Con: Higher cross-region egress & higher variance on tail latency.
- Throughput: baseline 12k tokens/sec per A100-80 profile GPU under continuous batching.
- SLA: 99.9% regional request availability; credits pro-rated.
- Discounts: 10% (3-month), 15% (12-month) for single-region commit. Multi-region stackable +5% for each additional region committed.

Option B — Isolated regional pools (recommended for GlobalPay)
- Per-region reserved pools (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) with optional DR replication layer.
- Pro: predictable latency, in-region logs, easier compliance.
- Con: higher baseline cost (estimated +25% vs Option A for same aggregate capacity).
- Replication: near-sync (hot) priced at +30% of per-region pool, warm-standby priced as +10% but with ~90s spin-up.
- Cross-region routing: optional managed failover at +8% of aggregate monthly commit (or pay egress + per-failover ops fee).
- Discounts: 12% (3-month), 22% (12-month) for full 3-region commit — subject to approval.

Ask: can we offer a 20–22% discount for a 12-month, 3-region commit? I'm proposing we hold at 22% if they take replication add-on and 12-month term. Otherwise, 18% baseline for 12-month.

Neha — good framing. A few commercial guardrails and edits: 

1) Discount guidance: approve up to 18% for a 12-month, 3-region commit as baseline. Approve incremental +4% (capped) if procurement accepts a replication add-on and 60-day payment terms. The full 22% ask is high without legal signoff on SLA terms and support uplift.

2) Replication pricing: prefer to list replication as an optional add-on with a clear TCO example (e.g., 30% add-on for hot near-sync but call out additional egress charges separately).

3) Cross-region routing: don't bundle as standard. Offer managed failover at a fixed percentage (8%) or as an a la carte feature. We should include an ops-runbook and one annual failover test as part of the managed failover SKU.

4) SLA and credits: require a maximum credit exposure cap (e.g., 100% of one month) to limit PS and infra risk. Also, call out latency SLOs per region with clear measurement window.

5) Approach to negotiation: present 2 commercial profiles to GlobalPay — "Performance-first (regional pools + hot replication)" and "Cost-first (shared pool + routing)". Include the MAP spreadsheet with real examples so procurement can see line-item math.

If you need legal pricing flexibility beyond 18%, loop in Markus (legal-commercial).

Rishi
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
